sectorSummary.overview: Affordable housing lending continued to grow, supported by distribution and productivity, but momentum and asset quality diverged. Home First maintained strong growth, while AAVAS indicated a lower FY27 AUM range and Aptus raised its credit-cost outlook; funding-cost transmission and insurance-income uncertainty require monitoring.

trends.text: AUM and disbursements continued to grow, with branch productivity and distribution supporting expansion.
Lenders are using technology, sourcing and collection processes to improve productivity while maintaining underwriting discipline.

tailwinds.text: Management continues to see demand from underserved homebuyers and scope to deepen existing markets.
Branch maturation and operating efficiency offer further scale benefits, although delivery varies by lender.

headwinds.text: Rising funding costs can precede asset repricing, creating pressure on spreads during transmission.
Potential insurance-distribution changes create uncertainty over fee income and mitigation through pricing or business mix.

opportunities.text: Home First is combining 27% AUM growth with lower operating cost/assets and stronger Stage 3 performance.
AAVAS targets higher relationship-officer productivity and lower medium-term operating cost/AUM.
Aadhar and India Shelter expect stronger H2 disbursement and improved normalization after the cheque-clearance transition.

risks.text: Aptus’s NBFC stress drove higher consolidated credit costs and a revised FY27 credit-cost view, with possible Q3 growth moderation.
India Shelter’s H1 credit cost is above its full-year target pace, making H2 recoveries important.
Weather, borrower cash-flow stress and smaller-ticket pockets require granular monitoring rather than assuming uniform sector deterioration.

insights.text: Aadhar and India Shelter distinguish reported growth from management-normalized figures after switching disbursement recognition to cheque clearance.
Aptus has begun separate HFC/NBFC disclosure; stronger HFC asset quality should not be attributed to the entire group.
Home First retains 25% FY27 AUM growth despite running above that rate in Q2; the annual target remains open.
